nodes.title: GWAS summary-stat files are often not sorted by position within a chromosome
nodes.summary: A GWAS parser that assumes sorted-by-position streaming will silently misassign SNPs to the wrong interval/locus when the input isn't actually sorted that way -- which is common for real GWAS files. Use an interval lookup structure instead of a sorted-streaming assumption so SNPs are assigned correctly regardless of file order.
nodes.trigger: writing a new parser that reads a GWAS summary-statistics file and assigns SNPs to loci/regions by position

nodes.title: Fingerprint-based staleness check to skip unnecessary reprocessing
nodes.summary: Hash the input file(s) + the relevant config + the pipeline/tool version together into one fingerprint per output; only reprocess when the fingerprint changes. Avoids rerunning expensive steps when nothing that could affect the output has actually changed, without needing a full dependency-graph system.

nodes.title: JSONP-wrapped static JSON files for CORS-free local-filesystem serving
nodes.summary: When a browser-based viewer needs to load many small per-item JSON files directly from the local filesystem (file:// URLs, no server), wrap each JSON payload in a JS function call (e.g. `loadLocus123({...})`) and load it via a <script> tag instead of fetch()/XHR -- script tags aren't subject to the same-origin/CORS restrictions that block local-file fetch() calls.
nodes.trigger: building a browser viewer that needs to load many separate JSON data files without running a server

nodes.title: Java `static final int` port constants get inlined — recompiling one file won't change other classes' printed values
nodes.summary: LocalServer.PORT is `public static final int PORT = 8765`, a compile-time constant. Recompiling only LocalServer.java with a new value (e.g. to test on a second port without touching the live server) correctly changes LocalServer's own runtime bind (InetSocketAddress uses the fresh value), but any other already-compiled class that references LocalServer.PORT (e.g. Main.java's startup printf) keeps the OLD value baked in at its call sites, because javac inlines static final primitive/String constants everywhere they're referenced, not just where they're declared. Symptom: the console log says 'Server at http://localhost:8765/' even though netstat shows it's actually listening on 8766. Verify the real bound port with netstat/ss, not by trusting printed log text, whenever only a subset of classes was recompiled.
nodes.trigger: Testing a Java app that hardcodes a port/value as `static final`, by recompiling just one file into a copied bin/ to run a second instance on a different port for verification.

nodes.title: LYNXgwas: raw GWAS input files get deleted post-processing, but .gz originals survive as siblings
nodes.summary: In this environment's fully-processed demo corpus (scz-full-demo/workspace and disease-demos/), each project's config.properties gwas.file points at a decompressed .tsv/.txt that no longer exists on disk (deleted after the earlier full-reprocessing pass to save space) — but a same-named .tsv.gz/.txt.gz sibling is still present one directory over (e.g. disease-demos/scz_extra/, disease-demos/t2d/, disease-demos/cad/, and scz-full-demo/PGC3_SCZ_full.tsv.gz). MultiLocusMerger/MultiLocusScanner (and presumably the single-project pipeline) read cfg.gwasFile directly and fail with a bare 'file not found' if only the .gz exists. Fix: `gunzip -k -f <the>.gz` to restore the exact decompressed filename the config expects, without touching/deleting the .gz. Needed before any locus-matrix / gene-constellation / multi-dataset run against 'already processed' projects in this corpus can actually execute for real (rather than replaying only previously-cached merged.tsv outputs).
nodes.trigger: A locus-matrix/gene-constellation (or any multi-project merge) run against the scz-full-demo / disease-demos corpus fails with '<file>.tsv (The system cannot find the file specified)'.
